summary.one_liner: Ralph for Claude Code is a Bash framework that runs Claude Code in an autonomous loop on a project until its task list is complete, with exit detection, rate limiting, and a circuit breaker to stop runaway loops.
summary.what_it_does: Installs global commands (ralph, ralph-monitor, ralph-setup, ralph-enable, ralph-import, ralph-queue, ralph-migrate, ralph-stats) that repeatedly invoke Claude Code against a project's .ralph/PROMPT.md and .ralph/fix_plan.md. Exit requires both heuristic completion indicators and an explicit EXIT_SIGNAL: true from Claude. Rate limiting caps calls per hour (default 100) and optionally tokens per hour, and a circuit breaker opens after no-progress or repeated-error thresholds. It can import requirements from PRD files or GitHub issues, process a batch queue of issues, and optionally run each iteration inside a Docker or E2B cloud sandbox. A tmux-based monitor and live streaming output provide visibility into the loop.
use_cases: run Claude Code autonomously overnight on a backlog of tasks
convert a PRD or spec document into a task list for an AI coding agent
import GitHub issues as work items for an automated coding loop
limit API call and token usage during unattended AI coding sessions
run AI coding iterations inside an isolated Docker container
monitor a long-running autonomous coding loop in tmux
notable: Dual-condition exit gate: completion indicators plus explicit EXIT_SIGNAL: true from Claude before stopping
Three-layer 5-hour API limit detection with auto-wait for unattended runs
Optional sections in fix_plan.md that do not block completion
Docker and E2B sandbox providers keep the loop on the host while Claude runs in isolation
Batch queue (ralph-queue) processes GitHub issues one at a time with priority and dependency ordering
caveats: Requires Bash 4.0+, Claude Code CLI, jq, git, and GNU coreutils timeout (macOS needs brew coreutils); tmux recommended
Unreleased change makes .ralphrc parsed as data, so older .ralphrc files using shell syntax break
Parallel queue processing is explicitly out of scope; items run one at a time on a single branch
E2B sandbox commits made inside the sandbox are not synced back; E2B cost is only estimated from runtime
